I thought this was going to be Presentation bug (like #84137) but I found something extremely interesting in that video that rules that out.

See the frames individually:
[smplayer_screenshots.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/19218545/smplayer_screenshots.zip)

02 & 03 are exactly the same frame. This indicates stutter. Could be caused by a presentation issue, or simply a performance issue that caused the GPU to miss a frame.
04 jumps forward.
05 jumps backwards, making it look like they were presented out of order. HOWEVER, look at the particle system (lower right corner). **It's still moving forward!** That rules out presentation issues (this makes me extremely happy).

**What could cause this?**

1. User Error. The user reported this is a game with a Server-Client model, thus it's possible that Server sent data out of order. If Client is doing client-side prediction, it's possible that the client overshot the prediction (which is totally plausible given that there was a genuine hiccup between frames 02 & 03) and then got corrected. While this happens all the time in Multiplayer models with client-side prediction, the problem tend to arise when ping > 100ms, not when there are sub 20ms hiccups.
2. Godot error: Following from the previous one, if the user is the one doing the prediction; the problem could be on how user relies on timing provided by Godot (and timing being messed up).
3. Godot error: if Godot is doing the client-side prediction, that's on us. (I've got no idea how the Multiplayer area works on Godot, I do rendering).
4. Godot error: Rendering. Objects' transforms. Something could be wrong in `_fill_instance_data` where we fill data of each object (but not the particle FX), or in `_setup_render_pass_uniform_set` where we create the set of uniforms to send to the GPU. I've been recently looking into this functions, and I can't see anything wrong yet.

Note that there are two separate issues:

1. Godot Forward+ causing stutter (and IIRC you said Mobile was doing it too?). This could be caused by various reasons, most likely an X11 or NVIDIA issue. Which goes away in Compatibility because it uses OpenGL. Sometimes the cause is power saving. Dario has had nasty issues from NVIDIA card going either at too low power (not enough to reach 60 fps even for a 4090) or too high (fans go full blast).
2. Most likely your code (though maybe something bad from Godot timing calculations) recovering extremely poorly from a single stutter caused by 1.

Regarding Godot's stutter: Could you post the output of `vulkaninfo`? I want to see there are no nasty implicit instance layers affecting Godot.

Another way to measure performance is via [MangoHud](https://github.com/flightlessmango/MangoHud). Running the app with environment variable MANGOHUD=1 should show an overlay, and pressing `Left Shift + F12` starts logging. Upload that log here too (you can control where the log is written in  `~/.config/MangoHud`) from a few seconds of gameplay while the stutter was captured. If the logs show uneven framerate while Godot said it was perfect 16.66ms, please do say so.

OK now I know with high certainty that it's a driver bug.

It's pretty clear NVIDIA is not respecting FIFO V-Sync. **Otherwise it'd be impossible to see 3 frames in a row taking 0.265ms in the middle of of frames taking roughly 16ms**. I'd understand 1 frame taking 0.265. Maybe 2. BUT 3? No, that's a bug. There's no way the GPU was stuck for 50ms without signaling the CPU to start processing one of the available swapchains.

It might be a HW issue with the motherboard or RAM timings, but they'd have to be the same model since you say both machines of yours are exhibiting the same problem. Sometimes messing with settings like ReBAR, HPET, or CSM vs UEFI makes a difference; as it interferes with how interrupts are fired (which the driver uses for the CPU to synchronize with the GPU). Perhaps a BIOS update fixes it (careful with BIOS updates, of course; it can brick your PC).

I see that one of your machines is plugged to 2 monitors. Are both machines plugged to two monitors? Perhaps that is a precondition to trigger the bug (given that a lot of people are unable to repro).

Have you tried installing the [NV driver from their website?](https://www.nvidia.com/en-in/drivers/) (i.e. instead of relying on the package in apt). At least the version that ships with Ubuntu is modified; I've had problems with it, while the NV version just works fine (but it's a PITA because it tends to break after an update and needs reinstalling).

Does the problem repro in a live usb? (assuming it boots with decently recent drivers).

If the problem can be easily reproduced in other machines, it could be sent to NVIDIA.

@darksylinc  @Calinou 

After installing Linux Mint Mate 22.1 the library asset example using the Forward+ renderer initially run well with vsync on with no stutter. Then later after setting up the things on Linux Mint the demo started stuttering again in exactly the same way as before. I decided to take a stab at trying Linux Mint Cinnamon 22.1 and then ran the library asset example with vsync on and no stutter at all. 

I next installed and launched the Linux CPU monitoring software CPU-X to monitor frequency scaling changes. I then ran the library asset example with vsync on and it instantly began to stutter. It was at that moment I made the connection to CPU 'Frequency' monitoring software and this Vulkan stuttering issue. I next exited CPU-X with the asset library example still running and the stuttering instantly disappeared. 

It turns out that any CPU frequency monitoring software running on Linux Mint was causing a cyclical stutter when a Godot (I assume other Vulkan apps too) application is using Vulkan. The stutter rate will match the polling rate of the CPU frequency monitoring software. I have tested this with Linux Mint Mate 21.1 and 22.1 as well as Linux Mint Cinnamon 22.1 and the issue exist on all these Linux Mint versions.

This issue is easily replicated by running a Godot 4.x application using Forward+ alongside Linux applications like CPU-X or Linux Mint’s Mate panel application ‘CPU Frequency Scaling Monitor’. With these applications running a cyclical delay or stutter is induced in the Vulkan render based on the polling rate of the CPU monitoring software. In my case, the panel app ‘CPU Frequency Scaling Monitor’ is the most insidious as I never thought a panel app could cause such an issue. I was using this panel app on all my systems which caused the stutter issue.

I have reopened this issue to add this information. I will close the issue baring any further discussion. It was an odyssey finding the cause to this issue. :)

They should be using [NVML instead](https://developer.nvidia.com/management-library-nvml).
